item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine is striking Russian strategic targets, including a drone strike that killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant and attacks on a St Petersburg missile-fuel plant, while Russia is hitting Ukrainian power facilities and the Northern Bridge with missiles and drones. Russia has begun rationing petrol after Ukrainian strikes damaged its second-largest refinery in Saratov, prompting Rosneft to cap sales, and a Russian FPV drone wounded three energy workers in Sumy Oblast. Leaked data suggest more than 400,000 Russian soldiers have been killed fighting in the war. The United Nations Security Council is monitoring the situation as trilateral peace talks involving the US, Russia and Ukraine begin in Abu Dhabi, and UCDP recorded 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Heavy rains are flooding tens of thousands of displacement tents across Gaza, damaging structures already weakened by bombings and prompting gunfire that struck tents at the Rafah site as aid teams prepare for winter storms. A sand embankment collapsed in Gaza, killing a woman and injuring several people. Israeli forces deported fourteen foreign pro-Palestinian activists arrested in the West Bank during the olive harvest and seized eight Palestinian homes in Jericho, displacing dozens of residents. The United Nations reported 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel and Hezbollah: the situation
item.description:
Israel has expanded its military footprint in southern Lebanon, constructing a 90km road network and opening new bases, while Hezbollah continues artillery fire on Israeli positions and has begun cash payments to war victims and displaced families. Israeli strikes have wounded a Lebanese footballer and led to the detention of a 65-year-old retired engineer, and French investigators are probing alleged Israeli war crimes in the area. The United Nations reports 300,000 people displaced in Lebanon, and protests against Israeli attacks have taken place in Sweden. The conflict caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
The United States carried out fresh strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island and disabled a commercial vessel attempting to run a blockade in the Gulf of Oman, while Iran launched a missile that struck a building in Tel Aviv. Iran continues to use the Strait of Hormuz as leverage, and the United States offered a $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear program. France warned of a response to a cyberattack on supermarkets blamed on Iran. The conflict has already caused 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthi forces maintain a month-long siege of Taiz while Yemeni government troops have seized the al-Jawf mountain range, intensifying front-line fighting. Houthi rockets damaged the Saudi Aramco tower in Riyadh and the coalition intercepted a cruise missile, a long-range anti-tank guided missile and downed a ballistic missile aimed at Medina. A Saudi strike near Sanaa killed 22 civilians, mostly women and children, and a Houthi-claimed airstrike near the capital also killed 22 people. The vital East-West pipeline was hit, prompting Saudi officials to inspect Aramco facilities, while Pakistan condemned the attacks and Syria announced troops to Saudi Arabia. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Jordan and Syria have deepened cooperation, signing eleven agreements covering economic projects, security coordination and a rail link, with officials saying bilateral ties are at their strongest in decades. Baghdad has reopened the Sheeb border crossing with Iran after a three-week closure and agreed to withdraw Turkish forces from the Zilkan base by the end of 2026. item.description:

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Al-Shabaab gunmen ambushed road construction workers on the Arabia-Lafey road in Mandera, killing eight, including two police reservists, and also stormed the Mjengo site, killing at least eight more. Somali security forces opened fire on protesters in Mogadishu, killing three civilians, while a former prime minister accused the government of cutting payments to 10,000 soldiers and families. President Mohamud declared fighting Al-Shabaab a top priority in Jowhar, and regional leaders warned of consequences if federal troops attack the Hiiraan region. Egypt, Somalia and Djibouti held talks reaffirming their exclusive role in securing the Red Sea waterway. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:

In Plateau, gunmen attacked two communities, killing five civilians, injuring two, and later killed a soldier and three locals in a separate assault. Police moved into a bandits' enclave in Sokoto and the army killed a suspected criminal and recovered an AK-47 in an Oyo forest where abducted schoolchildren had been held. An APC chieftain was killed by his son with a sledgehammer in Edo, and a son of a former Kaduna governor condemned an attack on NDC supporters in Delta. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Libya and Chad signed the final document of the CEN-SAD Executive Council meeting, and Egypt is seeking faster progress on Libya gas, refining and power projects.
